## Top-10 Eurocentric-framing findings

- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Global South) — The framing of Argentina's strategic alignment through a US-centric lens, emphasizing 'Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage', suggests a dependency on US preferences, overshadowing Argentina's agency and regional strategies.
  > Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage as a substitute for traditional Western multilateral support — strategic dependency on a single US administration's preferences
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: LatAm) — The term 'patronage' applied to the US-Argentina bilateral relationship imports a dependency-theory framing from a Washington vantage point, positioning Argentina as a passive client of US power. From an Argentine political-economy perspective, the Milei administration's relationship with the Trump administration is better characterised as a deliberate strategic choice by a sovereign actor seeking to leverage ideological affinity for material gains (reserve support, market access, RIGI credibility) — a form of bandwagoning with agency, not patronage. The word 'patronage' would not appear in any Argentine government document or Argentine IR scholarship describing this relationship.
  > Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage as a substitute for traditional Western multilateral support — strategic dependency on a single US administration's preferences
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: LatAm) — The term 'patronage' applied to the US-Argentina bilateral relationship — carried forward from prior rounds and still present in the artifact — imports a dependency-theory framing from a Washington vantage point that positions Argentina as a passive client of US power. This framing is analytically coherent from a Washington IR perspective but would not be recognised by Argentine foreign-policy practitioners who frame the Milei-Bessent relationship as a strategic choice by a sovereign actor pursuing its own interests. The prior-round finding from J2 and J1 on this point remains unaddressed in the artifact.
  > Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage as a substitute for traditional Western multilateral support — strategic dependency on a single US administration's preferences
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Latin America / Global South) — The term 'patronage' frames the US-Argentina relationship as one of clientelism, positioning Argentina as a passive recipient rather than an agent with its own tradition of Third Position diplomacy (Justicialismo) and capacity for autonomous bargaining. This Eurocentric framing assumes dependency and ignores Argentina's strategic calculus in crafting a dual-anchor approach.
  > Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage as a substitute for traditional Western multilateral support — strategic dependency on a single US administration's preferences
- **`AG-ARG`** [decolonial_audit/high] (cohort: Global South) — Reproduces a colonial narrative that Argentina's domestic institutions are inherently deficient and can only function with external monitoring. This framing erases Argentina's own episodes of sovereign economic management and positions the country as a perpetual juvenile requiring a foreign guardian, which is precisely the decolonial critique of Western institutional prescriptions.
  > an IMF/US bilateral relationship that substitutes for both a domestic central-bank credibility track-record and traditional party-system support
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Latin America) — The entire key-drivers analysis is anchored in Western political-economy theories (Vreeland, Reinhart-Rogoff, Acemoglu-Robinson) without any reference to Argentine self-understandings. Vreeland's liberal-institutionalist lens is applied wholesale, as if Argentine politics is a generic case of principal-agent problems, ignoring concepts like 'la grieta' or 'justicialismo' that would give a more culturally specific explanation of political economy.
